The Twin City Concept. - We stated in the Interim Report that this Commission has recognized the economic and social fact that two adjacent municipalities, being separate political entities, can be in reality a single commercial unit. We noted that commercial zone definitions traditionally have taken this fact into consideration. No evidence has been submitted in this proceeding to warrant a different approach. Therefore, the following sets of cities which have traditionally been considered twin cities shall continue to have a single uniform commercial zone measuring from the outer boundaries of each of the involved municipalities and using the combined population of the involved municipalities: (1) St. Louis, Mo.-East St. Louis, Ill, (2) Kansas City, Mo.,-Kansas City, Kans., (3) Davenport, Iowa, and Rock Island and Moline, Ill., (4) Minneapolis-St. Paul, Minn., (5) Bluefield, Va.-W. Va., (6) Bristol, Va.-Tenn., (7) Delmar, Del.-Md., (8) Harrison, Ohio-West Harrison, Ind., (9) Junction City, Ark.-La., (10) Texarkana, Ark.-Tex., (11) Texhoma, Tex.-Okla., and (12) Union City, Ind.-Ohio.
In response to this finding of the Interim Report, shipper and local interests in several other sets of cities have requested that their cities be considered as twin cities. These cities are (1) San Francisco-Oakland, Calif., (2) Cincinnati, Ohio, and Covington and Newport, Ky., and (3) Tampa-St. Petersburg, Fla.
